Hence it is added: [[2:20|who with sincere affection|qui sincera affectione]], that is, with pure and spiritual love, [[2:20|is solicitous for you|pro vobis sollicitus sit]].

paras.t: Omnes enim mecum existentes hac vice, id est tam multi eorum, ut alii comparatione eorum pene nulli videantur. Tales autem locutiones, hyperbolicæ sunt, in quibus dicitur aliquid per excessum. Omnes ergo quæ sua sunt, id est propria lucra, quærunt potius quam quæ Jesu Christi, id est, Dei honorem et gloriam non requirunt, principaliter atque finaliter. Multi enim mercenarii erant cum Paulo hoc tempore.
paras.en: [[2:21|For all|Omnes enim]] who are with me at this time, that is, so many of them that the others seem next to none in comparison. Such expressions are hyperbolic, in which something is said by way of excess. All, then, [[2:21|seek|quærunt]] [[2:21|the things that are their own|quæ sua sunt]], that is, their own gains, rather than [[2:21|the things that are Jesus Christ's|quæ Jesu Christi]], that is, they do not seek the honour and glory of God principally and as their end. For there were many hirelings with Paul at this time.

paras.t: Experimentum autem ejus cognoscite, id est, per experientiam vitæ et prædicationis probate verum esse quod de laudibus Timothei disserui : quod veraciter dixi, vosque experiri poteritis; quoniam sicut patri filius servit, sic mecum servivit Deo in Evangelio, id est in prædicatione, defensione et confirmatione, ceterisque actibus evangelicæ legis.
paras.en: [[2:22|Now know ye the proof of him|Experimentum autem ejus cognoscite]], that is, prove by experience of his life and preaching that what I have set out in praise of Timothy is true: that I have spoken truly, and you will be able to find it by experience; [[2:22|that as a son with the father|quoniam sicut patri filius]] (that is, as a son serves his father), [[2:22|so hath he served with me|sic mecum servivit]] God [[2:22|in the gospel|in Evangelio]], that is, in preaching, defending and confirming it, and in the other works of the law of the Gospel.

paras.t: Hunc igitur tam idoneum nuntium, spero me mittere ad vos, mox quum videro quæ circa me sunt, id est, quum expertus fuerim, seu alio modo cognoverim, quem exitum sortientur ea quæ mihi jam acciderunt. Interim nempe carere non possum præsentia Timothei. Confido autem in Domino quoniam et ipse veniam ad vos cito, quia de carcere isto liberari, in Græciamque reverti confido.
paras.en: [[2:23|Him therefore|Hunc igitur]], so fit a messenger, [[2:23|I hope to send unto you immediately|spero me mittere ad vos, mox]]: [[2:23|so soon as I shall see how it will go with me|quum videro quæ circa me sunt]], that is, when I have found out by experience, or come to know in some other way, what outcome the things that have now befallen me will have. For in the meantime I cannot do without Timothy's presence. [[2:24|And I trust in the Lord that I myself also shall come to you shortly|Confido autem in Domino quoniam et ipse veniam ad vos cito]], because I am confident of being freed from this prison and of returning to Greece.

paras.t: Necessarium autem, id est vestræ saluti multum expediens, existimavi Epaphroditum diaconum, præsentis epistolæ portitorem, fratrem religione, et cooperatorem in Evangelii prædicatione ac observatione, et commilitonem meum in persecutione et luctatione pro fide, vestrum autem apostolum, id est instructorem præcipuum, et ministrum necessitatis meæ, id est servitorem meum, præbentem mihi necessaria in hac mei incarceratione, quoniam munera vestra detulit mihi, quibus eo ministrante sustentatus sum, mittere ad vos cum hac epistola, ante missionem Timothei. Et merito, quoniam quidem omnes vos desiderabat videre et consolari ; et mæstus erat propterea, id est de hoc, quod audieratis illum infirmatum, sicut et fuit. Doluit autem quod ipsi hoc perceperunt, sciens eos sibi compati, et de ejus morte angustiari. Unde eorum compassioni et curæ condoluit.
paras.en: [[2:25|But I have thought it necessary|Necessarium autem]], that is, very expedient for your salvation, [[2:25|to send to you|mittere ad vos]] [[2:25|Epaphroditus|Epaphroditum]] the deacon, the bearer of the present letter, [[2:25|my brother|fratrem]] in religion, [[2:25|and fellow labourer|et cooperatorem]] in preaching and keeping the Gospel, [[2:25|and fellow soldier|et commilitonem meum]] in persecution and in the struggle for the faith, [[2:25|but your apostle|vestrum autem apostolum]], that is, your chief instructor, [[2:25|and he that hath ministered to my wants|et ministrum necessitatis meæ]], that is, my servant, who provides me with what I need in this imprisonment of mine, since he brought me your gifts[[Phil 4:18||]], by which I have been sustained through his ministry; to send him to you with this letter, before sending Timothy. And rightly so, [[2:26|for indeed he longed after you all|quoniam quidem omnes vos desiderabat]], to see and comfort you: [[2:26|and was sad|et mæstus erat]], [[2:26|for that|propterea]], that is, for this, [[2:26|you had heard that he was sick|quod audieratis illum infirmatum]], as indeed he was. He grieved that they had learned of it, knowing that they suffered with him and were distressed at the thought of his death. Hence he grieved at their compassion and concern.

paras.t: Nam et infirmatus est usque ad mortem exclusive; sed Deus misertus est ejus, ipsum clementer sanando. Unde patet, vitam animæ in corpore non penitus esse innaturalem, et velut in carcere, ut quidam dixerunt. Non solum autem ejus misertus est Deus, verum etiam et mei misertus est, liberando me ab interiori dolore, ne tristitiam de morte Epaphroditi super tristitiam de vestri desolatione haberem. Quamvis enim tristitia hæc in se bona fuisset, eo quod inordinata tristitia in Apostolo locum non habuit, juxta illud Sapientis, Non contristabit justum quidquid ei acciderit ; Deus tamen convertit eam in melius, sicut Salvator promisit, Tristitia vestra vertetur in gaudium.
paras.en: [[2:27|For indeed he was sick, nigh unto death|Nam et infirmatus est usque ad mortem]], exclusively [that is, to the very edge of death, but not into it]; [[2:27|but God had mercy on him|sed Deus misertus est ejus]], healing him in his clemency. Hence it is plain that the life of the soul in the body is not wholly unnatural, as if it were in a prison, as some have said. [[2:27|And not only on him|Non solum autem ejus]] did God have mercy, [[2:27|but on me also|verum etiam et mei]] he had mercy, freeing me from inward grief, [[2:27|lest I should have sorrow|ne tristitiam]] at the death of Epaphroditus [[2:27|upon sorrow|super tristitiam]] at your desolation. For although this sorrow would have been good in itself, since inordinate sorrow had no place in the Apostle, according to that saying of the Wise Man, [[Prov 12:21|Whatsoever shall befall the just man, shall not make him sad|Non contristabit justum quidquid ei acciderit]]; yet God turned it to the better, as the Saviour promised, [[John 16:20|your sorrow shall be turned into joy|Tristitia vestra vertetur in gaudium]].

paras.t: Festinantius ergo, id est multum festinanter, misi illum ad vos, ut viso eo sano ac læto, iterum gaudeatis, gratias Domino referentes de sanatione ac reditu tam dilecti doctoris, et patris atque apostoli vestri, et ego sine tristitia sim, quum sciero vos consolatos, quorum desolationi condolui.
paras.en: [[2:28|Therefore|ergo]] [[2:28|the more speedily|Festinantius]], that is, in great haste, [[2:28|I sent him|misi illum]] to you, [[2:28|that seeing him|ut viso eo]] healthy and glad, [[2:28|again, you may rejoice|iterum gaudeatis]], giving thanks to the Lord for the healing and return of so beloved a teacher, your father and apostle, [[2:28|and I may be without sorrow|et ego sine tristitia sim]], when I know that you are comforted, whose desolation I grieved over.

paras.t: Excipite itaque illum cum omni gaudio spirituali, in Domino, id est Deum laudando ; et ejusmodi, id est virum talem ac tantum, cum honore habetote, id est, reverenter tractate. Qui enim bene præsunt, duplici honore digni sunt.
paras.en: [[2:29|Receive him therefore with all joy|Excipite itaque illum cum omni gaudio]], spiritual joy, [[2:29|in the Lord|in Domino]], that is, praising God; and [[2:29|such as he is|ejusmodi]], that is, a man of such a kind and so great, [[2:29|treat with honour|cum honore habetote]], that is, deal with him reverently. For they [[1 Tim 5:17|that rule well|Qui enim bene præsunt]] are [[1 Tim 5:17|worthy of double honour|duplici honore digni sunt]].

paras.t: Quoniam propter opus Christi, id est ad faciendum ea quæ Dei sunt, usque ad mortem accessit, id est, mortis periculo se exposuit, tradens animam suam, id est vitam suam morti exponens propter justitiam, ut impleret id quod ex vobis deerat, id est, actualem administrationem substantiæ mihi a vobis transmissæ, quam nullus vestrum coram mihi distribuit, ipse impenderet, erga meum obsequium, mihi personaliter ministrando.
paras.en: [[2:30|Because for the work of Christ|Quoniam propter opus Christi]], that is, to do the things that are God's, [[2:30|he came to the point of death|usque ad mortem accessit]], that is, exposed himself to the danger of death, [[2:30|delivering his life|tradens animam suam]], that is, exposing his life to death for justice' sake, [[2:30|that he might fulfil that which on your part was wanting|ut impleret id quod ex vobis deerat]]: that is, that he himself might carry out the actual dispensing of the goods sent me by you, which none of you dispensed to me in person, [[2:30|towards my service|erga meum obsequium]], by ministering to me in person.

3.title: EXPOSITIO CAPITULI TERTII : DE CETERO, FRATRES MEI, GAUDETE IN DOMINO.
3.title_en: Exposition of the third chapter: As to the rest, my brethren, rejoice in the Lord.

paras.t: Præterea monet ac munit Apostolus Philippenses contra pseudoapostolorum fallacias, qui eos ad legalium observantiam nitebantur inducere. De cetero, id est, post exhortationes præhabitas, hortor reliquo tempore, o fratres mei, gaudete in Domino, non in cærimonialibus legis. Eadem vobis scribere in præsenti epistola, quæ præsens dixeram vobis, videlicet non esse gaudendum nisi in fide et gratia Dei, atque legalia omitti debere, mihi quidem vos amanti non est pigrum, id est molestum aut tardum. Fervido enim amatori delectabile est operari quidquid dilecto salubre est. Vobis autem necessarium est hæc scribi, propter imminentia mala fallacium.
paras.en: Besides this, the Apostle warns and arms the Philippians against the deceits of the false apostles, who were striving to lead them into the observance of the legal ceremonies. [[3:1|As to the rest|De cetero]], that is, after the exhortations given above, I exhort you for the time remaining, O [[3:1|my brethren|fratres mei]], [[3:1|rejoice in the Lord|gaudete in Domino]], not in the ceremonies of the law. [[3:1|To write the same things to you|Eadem vobis scribere]] in the present epistle which I had told you when I was present, namely that we must not rejoice except in faith and the grace of God, and that the legal observances ought to be given up, [[3:1|to me indeed|mihi quidem]], who love you, [[3:1|is not wearisome|non est pigrum]], that is, irksome or slow. For to a fervent lover it is a delight to do whatever is wholesome for the one he loves; [[3:1|but to you is necessary|Vobis autem necessarium]] that these things be written, because of the evils of the deceivers that hang over you.

paras.t: Videte canes, id est pseudo, hæreticos, more canum rabido ore contra veritatem latrantes, videte malos operarios, id est pestiferos aliorum corruptores, videte concisionem, id est illos a Christo excisos, qui alios quoque a Christo dividere satagunt. Hos ergo attendite et cavete. Nos sumus Christifideles, […] id est vere ac spiritualiter circumcisi a vitiis, qui spiritu Dei, id est Spiritu Sancto movente, Deo Trinitati servimus servitute latriæ, quæ soli Deo debetur, […] in Christo Jesu, id est in virtute et gratia ac merito Christi, et non in carne fiduciam habentes, id est, non in carnalibus observantiis legis spem salutis constituentes : […]tiam in carne, id est, confidentiam talem haberem, si esset habenda. Vel, habeo eam, non ita ut in carnalibus sistam, sed ea ad Christi honorem omittam, sicque præmium consequar de hoc quod aliquando legalia observavi, quando merito ter servatu[…]
paras.en: [[3:2|Beware of dogs|Videte canes]], that is, false men, heretics, barking against the truth with rabid mouth after the manner of dogs; [[3:2|beware of evil workers|videte malos operarios]], that is, pestilent corrupters of others; [[3:2|beware of the concision|videte concisionem]], that is, those cut off from Christ, who busy themselves to divide others also from Christ [concisio, a cutting off, set against circumcisio, circumcision]. Mark these, therefore, and beware of them. As for us, [[3:3|we are|Nos sumus]] the faithful of Christ, […] that is, truly and spiritually circumcised from vices [the lost word is presumably the lemma circumcisio, the circumcision], [[3:3|who in spirit|qui spiritu]] of God, that is, by the moving of the Holy Ghost, [[3:3|serve|servimus]] God the Trinity with the service of latria, which is owed to God alone, […] [[3:3|in Christ Jesus|in Christo Jesu]], that is, in the power and grace and merit of Christ [the lost words are presumably the lemma et gloriamur, and glory], [[3:3|not having confidence in the flesh|et non in carne fiduciam habentes]], that is, not setting our hope of salvation in the carnal observances of the law: […] in the flesh, that is, I should have such confidence, if it were to be had [the lemma here, lost in part, reads quamquam ego habeam confidentiam et in carne, Though I might also have confidence in the flesh]. Or: I have it, not so as to rest in carnal things, but so as to give them up for the honour of Christ, and thus I shall obtain a reward for having once kept the legal observances, at the time when they were kept with merit […] [the Latin reads merito ter servatu…, and the rest is lost].

paras.t: Si quis alius deceptor videtur confidere in carne, id est carnali custodia legis et Israeliticæ stirpis dignitate, ego magis confidere possum (secundum sensum prætactum), videlicet quum sim circumcisus octavo die, ut lex Moysis jubet, natus ex genere Israel, id est genere Jacob, de tribu Benjamin filii Jacob, Hebræus natione ex Hebræis parentibus ortus, non proselytus; secundum legem, id est religiosam legis observantiam, Pharisæus, id est unus de præcipuis inter Judæos. Pharisæi enim dicebantur quasi contemptibili plebi non admixti, sed a communibus separati : sicut egregii, quasi a grege divisi dicuntur. Eratque secta Pharisæorum conformior legi, quam Sadducæorum, qui nec spiritum nec resurrectionem ponebant; et Essæorum, qui austerissimæ vitæ fuerunt, sed idiotæ. Secundum æmulationem, id est inordinatum affectum, videlicet secundum zelum non adjunctum scientiæ, quo persecutus est Ecclesiam Dei primitivam, ut patet in Actibus Apostolorum. Secundum justitiam quæ in lege est, conversatus sine querela, id est sine reprehensione custodiendo mandata legalia.
paras.en: [[3:4|If any other|Si quis alius]] deceiver [[3:4|thinketh he may have confidence in the flesh|videtur confidere in carne]], that is, in the carnal keeping of the law and the dignity of Israelite stock, [[3:4|I more|ego magis]] can have confidence (in the sense touched on above), since I am [[3:5|circumcised|circumcisus]] [[3:5|the eighth day|octavo die]], as the law of Moses commands[[Lev 12:3||]], born [[3:5|of the stock of Israel|ex genere Israel]], that is, of the race of Jacob, [[3:5|of the tribe of Benjamin|de tribu Benjamin]], the son of Jacob, [[3:5|an Hebrew|Hebræus]] by nation, sprung from Hebrew parents, not a proselyte; [[3:5|According to the law|secundum legem]], that is, in the devout observance of the law, [[3:5|a Pharisee|Pharisæus]], that is, one of the foremost among the Jews. For the Pharisees were so called as being not mixed with the contemptible common people but separated from ordinary men: just as the egregii [outstanding men] are so called as being set apart from the flock [e grege, out of the flock]. And the sect of the Pharisees was more in keeping with the law than that of the Sadducees, who held neither spirit nor resurrection[[Acts 23:8||]], and that of the Essenes, who were of a most austere life, but unlearned. [[3:6|According to zeal|Secundum æmulationem]], that is, an inordinate affection, namely according to a zeal not joined to knowledge[[Rom 10:2||]], with which he persecuted the primitive [[3:6|church of God|Ecclesiam Dei]], as is plain in the Acts of the Apostles[[Acts 8:3||]]. [[3:6|According to the justice that is in the law|Secundum justitiam quæ in lege est]], [[3:6|conversing without blame|conversatus sine querela]], that is, without reproach, keeping the commandments of the law.

paras.t: Sed quæ mihi erant lucra, id est, quæ commoda mihi erant tempore Judaismi, videlicet cærimonialia legis, hæc post conversionem meam ad fidem propter Christum, id est propter Christi amorem, doctrinam ac jussionem, detrimenta, id est nociva. Non enim servanda sunt cærimonialia legis post divulgationem evangelicæ veritatis, præsertim ut salus aliqua in illis esse credatur. Erant enim figurativa Christi : unde veritate impleta, cessare debebant.
paras.en: [[3:7|But the things that were gain to me|Sed quæ mihi erant lucra]], that is, the things that were advantages to me in the time of Judaism, namely the ceremonies of the law, [[3:7|the same|hæc]], after my conversion to the faith, I count [[3:7|for Christ|propter Christum]], that is, for the love, the teaching and the command of Christ, [[3:7|loss|detrimenta]], that is, harmful. For the ceremonies of the law are not to be kept after the gospel truth has been made known, least of all so that any salvation should be believed to lie in them. For they were figures of Christ: hence, once the truth was fulfilled, they had to cease.

paras.t: […]mentum esse, id est descerenda, propter eminentem, id est supernaturalem et præcellentem, scientiam Domini nostri Jesu Christi, id est, quam Christus nobis infundit per Spiritus Sancti illustrationem. Quod intelligi potest de scientia illa quæ est unum septem donorum Spiritus Sancti, vel de cognitione Christi beatifica quæ datur electis in patria, vel de quotidiana illustratione æternæ sapientiæ quæ in animas sanctas se transfert, rivos ac radios veræ sapientiæ studiosis ac piis cordibus liberaliter influens. Ob hanc scientiam adipiscendam, sobrie vivere, cunctaque sensibilia aspernari debemus. Propter quem Christum, id est ob cujus amorem ac gloriam obtinendam, omnia jam præfata detrimentum feci, id est, contemnenda monstravi, contempsi ac despici feci, et arbitror ea ut stercora, id est, pro nihilo reputavi, ut Christum lucrifaciam, id est, eum pro præmio adipiscar. Simile est quod in Sapientia dicitur : Divitias nihil esse dixi in comparatione illius.
paras.en: […] [[3:8|to be but loss|mentum esse]] [the lost words are presumably the lemma Verumtamen existimo omnia detri-, Furthermore, I count all things], that is, to be cast off, [[3:8|for the excellent|propter eminentem]], that is, supernatural and surpassing, [[3:8|knowledge of Jesus Christ, my Lord|scientiam Domini nostri Jesu Christi]], that is, the knowledge which Christ pours into us through the enlightening of the Holy Ghost. This can be understood of that knowledge which is one of the seven gifts of the Holy Ghost[[Is 11:2||]] [the margin gives Is. vi, 2; the seven gifts are named in Is 11:2], or of the beatific knowledge of Christ which is given to the elect in the fatherland, or of the daily enlightening by the eternal wisdom, which [[Wis 7:27|conveyeth herself into holy souls|in animas sanctas se transfert]], pouring streams and rays of true wisdom freely into studious and devout hearts. To gain this knowledge we must live soberly and spurn all things of sense. And [[3:8|for whom|Propter quem]], that is, for Christ, for love of whom and to obtain whose glory, [[3:8|I have suffered the loss of all things|omnia jam præfata detrimentum feci]] named above, that is, I have shown them to be contemptible, have contemned them and caused them to be despised, [[3:8|and count them but as dung|et arbitror ea ut stercora]], that is, I have reckoned them as nothing, [[3:8|that I may gain Christ|ut Christum lucrifaciam]], that is, obtain him as my reward. Like this is what is said in Wisdom: I [[Wis 7:8|esteemed riches nothing in comparison of her|Divitias nihil esse dixi in comparatione illius]].

paras.t: Et inveniar in illo, id est, Christo incorporer, ejusque membrum sim, non habens meam justitiam quæ ex lege est, id est justitiam quæ consistit in litterali observatione cærimonialium legis, quæ tempore novæ legis non est vera justitia, sed illam justitiam quæ ex fide est Jesu Christi, id est, quantum ad actum suum ex fide procedit, et in ea fundatur, non in operibus legis ; quæ justitia ex Deo est per creationem. Hæc enim est justitia infusa, quantum ad habitum, simulque cum fide infunditur, quamvis secundum ordinem naturæ eam præsupponat, quoniam fides basis seu fundamentum est universarum virtutum. Ideo subditur : justitia in fide, id est, justitia ista in fide consistit : quæ fides utilis est ad cognoscendum illum, videlicet Christum in præsenti per donum sapientiæ, in patria autem per speciem; ad cognoscendum etiam et virtutem resurrectionis ejus, id est potestatem resurrectionis Christi : cujus resurrectionis tanta est virtus, ut sit causa exemplaris resurrectionis omnium electorum. Valet etiam fides ad cognoscendum et societatem passionum illius, id est, ut sciamus quomodo crucem nostram post Christum portemus, ejusque passionibus communicemus ac sociemur.
paras.en: [[3:9|And may be found in him|Et inveniar in illo]], that is, may be incorporated into Christ and be his member, [[3:9|not having my justice, which is of the law|non habens meam justitiam quæ ex lege est]], that is, the justice which consists in the literal observance of the ceremonies of the law, which in the time of the new law is not true justice[[Rom 3:20||]], [[3:9|but that which is of the faith of Christ Jesus|sed illam justitiam quæ ex fide est Jesu Christi]], that is, which as to its act proceeds from faith and is founded on it, not on the works of the law; [[3:9|which is of God|quæ justitia ex Deo est]] by creation [that is, it is produced in the soul by God, not acquired by our own acts]. For this is infused justice as to the habit [a settled disposition of the soul], and it is infused together with faith, although in the order of nature it presupposes faith, since faith is the base or foundation of all the virtues. Therefore he adds: [[3:9|justice in faith|justitia in fide]], that is, this justice consists in faith: which faith is of use (as he goes on) [[3:10|That I may know him|ad cognoscendum illum]], namely Christ, in this present life by the gift of wisdom, but in the fatherland [that is, in heaven] by sight; for knowing also [[3:10|and the power of his resurrection|et virtutem resurrectionis ejus]], that is, the might of Christ's resurrection: and so great is the power of that resurrection that it is the exemplary cause of the resurrection of all the elect. Faith avails also for knowing [[3:10|and the fellowship of his sufferings|et societatem passionum illius]], that is, so that we may know how to carry our cross after Christ[[Luke 9:23||]], and share and be made partners in his sufferings.

paras.t: Inveniar ergo in Christo configuratus morti ejus, id est Christo compassus, vel propter illum occisus, aut propter justitiam tribulatus, vel per opera pœnitentiæ quotidie mortificatus, si quo modo, id est ad hoc ut aliquo modo, licet difficili, occurram in die judicii Christo et Sanctis, pertingendo ad resurrectionem quæ est ex mortuis, id est ad resurrectionem beatam, qua electi feliciter immutabuntur. Omnes namque resurgemus, sed non omnes immutabimur. Per resurrectionem ergo ex mortuis, hoc loco intelligitur resurrectio gloriosa, qua electi a reprobis discernentur, et ex eorum loco, qui terra est, in aera erigentur. Rapientur namque in nubibus obviam Christo in aera, sicut alibi dixit Apostolus.
paras.en: Let me be found, then, in Christ, [[3:10|being made conformable to his death|configuratus morti ejus]], that is, suffering with Christ, or slain for him, or afflicted for justice' sake, or mortified daily by works of penance, [[3:11|If by any means|si quo modo]], that is, so that in some way, though a hard one, [[3:11|I may attain|occurram]] at the day of judgement to Christ and the Saints [occurram: literally, run to meet], reaching [[3:11|to the resurrection which is from the dead|ad resurrectionem quæ est ex mortuis]], that is, to the blessed resurrection, in which the elect will be happily changed. [[1 Cor 15:51|We shall all indeed rise again: but we shall not all be changed|Omnes namque resurgemus, sed non omnes immutabimur]]. By the resurrection from the dead, then, is meant in this place the glorious resurrection, in which the elect will be set apart from the reprobate, and raised up from their place, which is the earth, into the air. For they shall be taken up [[1 Thess 4:16|in the clouds to meet Christ, into the air|in nubibus obviam Christo in aera]], as the Apostle has said elsewhere.

paras.t: Non quod jam acceperim, id est, non ideo dixi tanta de mea perfectione, qua omnia propter Christum ut stercora reputo, quasi jam plenam perfectionem adeptus sim, vel futuram felicitatem nunc actualiter habeam : ideo subditur, aut jam perfectus sim in tantum ut ultra proficere nequeam. Aliquo tamen modo perfectus fuit Apostolus, quia post pauca adjecit : Quicumque ergo perfecti sumus.
paras.en: [[3:12|Not as though I had already attained|Non quod jam acceperim]], that is, I have not said such great things of my perfection, by which I count all things as dung for Christ, as though I had already gained full perfection, or now actually possessed the happiness to come: therefore he adds, [[3:12|or were already perfect|aut jam perfectus sim]], so far that I could advance no further. Yet in some way the Apostle was perfect, for a little after he adds: [[3:15|Let us therefore, as many as are perfect|Quicumque ergo perfecti sumus]].

paras.t: Sequor autem, id est, ad perfectionem tendo affectibus cordis et bonis operibus potius quam gressibus corporis, si quo modo, id est ut tandem aliquando, comprehendam Christum comprehensione beatificæ visionis, de qua ipse ait : Manifestabo ei me ipsum, videlicet secundum divinam naturam; in quo, id est eo modo cognitionis seu tali claritate notitiæ, et comprehensus sum, id est perfecte cognitus, a Christo Jesu. Unde alibi dicit Apostolus : Videmus nunc per speculum in ænigmate, tunc autem facie ad faciem. Et nunc, inquit, cognosco ex parte, tunc autem cognoscam sicut et cognitus sum. Nulla tamen creatura pura potest Deum comprehendere plene et absolute; sed comprehensio sumitur tunc pro clara notitia alicujus secundum suam essentiam : sicque Beati in patria comprehensores vocantur. Propter quod ait Joannes : Similes ei erimus, quia videbimus eum sicuti est.
paras.en: [[3:12|I follow after|Sequor autem]], that is, I tend towards perfection by the affections of the heart and by good works rather than by the steps of the body, [[3:12|if I may by any means|si quo modo]], that is, so that at length some day, I may [[3:12|apprehend|comprehendam]] Christ with the apprehension of the beatific vision, of which he himself says: I [[John 14:21|will manifest myself to him|Manifestabo ei me ipsum]], namely according to the divine nature; [[3:12|wherein|in quo]], that is, in that manner of knowledge, or with such clearness of knowing, [[3:12|I am also apprehended|et comprehensus sum]], that is, perfectly known, [[3:12|by Christ Jesus|a Christo Jesu]]. Hence the Apostle says elsewhere: [[1 Cor 13:12|We see now through a glass in a dark manner: but then face to face|Videmus nunc per speculum in ænigmate, tunc autem facie ad faciem]]. And now, he says, [[1 Cor 13:12|I know in part: but then I shall know even as I am known|cognosco ex parte, tunc autem cognoscam sicut et cognitus sum]]. Yet no mere creature can comprehend God fully and absolutely; but comprehension is taken here for a clear knowledge of a thing according to its essence: and so the Blessed in the fatherland are called comprehensors [the theologians' name for the blessed, who have reached the goal, as against wayfarers still on the road]. Hence John says: [[1 John 3:2|we shall be like to him: because we shall see him as he is|Similes ei erimus, quia videbimus eum sicuti est]].

paras.t: Fratres, ego me non arbitror comprehendisse arcem virtutum perfectionisque apicem, præsertim quum dicat Salvator : Quum feceritis omnia quæ præcepta sunt vobis, dicite : Servi inutiles sumus ; quod debuimus facere, fecimus. Et iterum alibi : Omnem qui fert fructum purgabit Pater, ut fructum plus afferat. Nondum igitur comprehendit, sed proficit. Hæc dicit de se ipso Apostolus, ne aliquis nostrum quantumcumque laudetur, vana elatione infletur, sed conetur proficere exemplo tanti Apostoli ; nec unquam dicere audeat, Sufficit mihi, quum non proficere, sit deficere. Nemo etiam erubescat imperfectum suum fateri, quum audiat Apostolum ista dicentem.
paras.en: [[3:13|Brethren, I do not count myself to have apprehended|Fratres, ego me non arbitror comprehendisse]] the stronghold of the virtues and the summit of perfection, above all since the Saviour says: [[Luke 17:10|when you shall have done all these things that are commanded you, say: We are unprofitable servants; we have done that which we ought to do|Quum feceritis omnia quæ præcepta sunt vobis, dicite : Servi inutiles sumus ; quod debuimus facere, fecimus]]. And again elsewhere: [[John 15:2|every one that beareth fruit, he will purge it|Omnem qui fert fructum purgabit]], the Father, [[John 15:2|that it may bring forth more fruit|ut fructum plus afferat]]. He has not yet apprehended, then, but is advancing. The Apostle says these things of himself so that none of us, however much he is praised, may be puffed up with vain elation, but may strive to advance after the example of so great an Apostle; and may never dare to say, It is enough for me, since not to advance is to fall back. Nor let anyone be ashamed to confess his imperfection, when he hears the Apostle saying these things.

paras.t: Et quasi sciscitaremur : Quid ergo facis, o Paule, et quid nobis agendum tuo exemplo demonstras? subjecit : Unum autem dico agendum, illudque facio, puta : quæ quidem retro sunt obliviscens, id est præcedentia merita mea parvi pendens nec pensans, sed memoriæ Dei commendans ; ad ea vero quæ sunt priora, id est ad opera perfectiora atque futura quæ nondum attigi, sed oculis meis proposui, extendens me ipsum, id est vires meas applicans per incessantem profectum.
paras.en: And as though we were asking, What then dost thou, O Paul, and what dost thou show us by thy example that we must do? he added: [[3:13|But one thing|Unum autem]] I say must be done, and this I do, namely: [[3:13|Forgetting the things that are behind|quæ quidem retro sunt obliviscens]], that is, making little of my past merits and not weighing them, but committing them to God's remembrance; [[3:13|to those that are before|ad ea vero quæ sunt priora]], that is, to the more perfect works still to come, which I have not yet reached but have set before my eyes, [[3:13|stretching forth myself|extendens me ipsum]], that is, applying my strength in unceasing progress.

paras.t: Vel sic : Quæ retro sunt, id est terrena, sensibilia, præsertim carnalia, obliviscens ac deserens, juxta illud, Obliviscere populum tuum et domum patris tui : ad ea vero quæ sunt priora, id est ad obtinenda, amanda et contemplanda bona cœlestia ac divina, extendens me ipsum ardenti affectu et digno effectu. Ad destinatum, id est finale bonum a me intentum, atque a Deo mihi paratum, persequor, id est, perfecte sequor, ut ipsum acquiram : sic ut et scriptum est, Inquire pacem, et persequere eam. De quo destinato adjicitur : ad bravium supernæ vocationis Dei, id est præmium vitæ cœlestis a Deo propositum ac promissum, in Christo Jesu, in quo et per quem vocati sumus ad bravium istud, per cujus etiam gratiam illud acquirimus. Bravium autem est quoddam præmium victoribus datum. Debemus autem semper ad hoc bravium tendere, ita ut omne quod agimus vel patimur, ad æternæ adeptionem beatitudinis ordinemus.
paras.en: Or thus: [[3:13|the things that are behind|Quæ retro sunt]], that is, earthly things, things of sense, above all carnal things, [[3:13|Forgetting|obliviscens]] and forsaking, according to that saying, [[Ps 44:11|forget thy people and thy father's house|Obliviscere populum tuum et domum patris tui]]; [[3:13|to those that are before|ad ea vero quæ sunt priora]], that is, to obtaining, loving and contemplating heavenly and divine goods, [[3:13|stretching forth myself|extendens me ipsum]] with ardent affection and worthy effect. [[3:14|towards the mark|Ad destinatum]], that is, the final good intended by me and prepared for me by God, [[3:14|I press|persequor]], that is, I follow perfectly, so as to gain it: as it is also written, [[Ps 33:15|seek after peace and pursue it|Inquire pacem, et persequere eam]] [persequor, I press on, is the same verb as persequere, pursue]. Of this mark he adds: [[3:14|to the prize of the supernal vocation of God|ad bravium supernæ vocationis Dei]], that is, the reward of heavenly life set before us and promised by God, [[3:14|in Christ Jesus|in Christo Jesu]], in whom and through whom we have been called to this prize, and by whose grace also we gain it. Now a bravium is a prize given to victors[[1 Cor 9:24||]]. And we ought always to tend towards this prize, so that we direct all that we do or suffer to the gaining of eternal happiness.

paras.t: Quicumque ergo perfecti sumus, id est, secundum exigentiam et possibilitatem hujus fragilis vitæ ad caritatis atque virtutum sinceritatem venerimus, passionibus reformatis et inimicis vere dilectis, prout Salvator hortatur : Estote perfecti sicut et Pater vester cœlestis perfectus est ; hoc sentiamus quod ego jam dixi, videlicet quod nondum apprehendimus perfectionem completam, eamque adipisci conemur. Et si quid aliter sapitis, id est, si sic sapiendum seu sentiendum esse non æstimatis ut dixi, nolentes vos penitus humiliare, et hoc vobis Deus revelabit esse erroneum, vel nunc per divinæ illustrationis gratiam, vel in futuro per pœnarum experientiam. Vel sic : Si quid aliter sapitis, id est, si alios modos proficiendi noveritis, et hoc vobis Deus revelabit, id est, hanc notitiam Deus dabit, eamque perficiet.
paras.en: [[3:15|Let us therefore, as many as are perfect|Quicumque ergo perfecti sumus]], that is, as many of us as have come, so far as the conditions and the powers of this frail life allow, to sincerity of charity and the virtues, with our passions reformed and our enemies truly loved, as the Saviour exhorts: [[Matt 5:48|Be you therefore perfect, as also your heavenly Father is perfect|Estote perfecti sicut et Pater vester cœlestis perfectus est]]; [[3:15|be thus minded|hoc sentiamus]], as I have said already, namely that we have not yet apprehended complete perfection, and let us strive to gain it. [[3:15|and if in any thing you be otherwise minded|Et si quid aliter sapitis]], that is, if you do not judge that one should think or feel as I have said, being unwilling to humble yourselves wholly, [[3:15|this also God will reveal to you|et hoc vobis Deus revelabit]] to be mistaken, either now by the grace of divine enlightening, or in the future by the experience of punishment. Or thus: [[3:15|if in any thing you be otherwise minded|Si quid aliter sapitis]], that is, if you know other ways of advancing, [[3:15|this also God will reveal to you|et hoc vobis Deus revelabit]], that is, God will give this knowledge and bring it to completion.

paras.t: Veruntamen ad quod pervenimus, id est in gradu perfectionis quem bene vivendo attigimus, stemus et proficiamus, ut idem sapiamus in his quæ ad salutem exiguntur, et fidem concernunt, et in eadem permaneamus regula, id est in pari rectitudine vitæ, seu in eadem lege et gratia nos regulante.
paras.en: [[3:16|Nevertheless, whereunto we are come|Veruntamen ad quod pervenimus]], that is, in the degree of perfection which we have reached by living well, let us stand and advance, [[3:16|that we be of the same mind|ut idem sapiamus]] in the things that are required for salvation and concern the faith, [[3:16|let us also continue in the same rule|et in eadem permaneamus regula]], that is, in a like uprightness of life, or in the same law and grace that rules us.

paras.t: Imitatores mei estote. In superioribus Apostolus proposuit se in exemplum ; nunc admonet ad se imitandum, dicendo : Imitatores mei estote, o fratres, id est, conformate vos mihi in præinductis virtutibus, atque in omni opere virtuoso, et observate, id est, solerter attendite et sequi curate, […] habetis formam nostram, id est virtuosos qui taliter conversantur sicut ego vobis verbo et opere manifestavi esse vivendum. Alios autem cavete. A fructibus enim eorum cognoscetis, an juxta formam vitæ nostræ conversantur, et imitatione sint condigni.
paras.en: [[3:17|Be ye followers of me|Imitatores mei estote]]. Above, the Apostle set himself forward as an example; now he urges them to imitate him, saying: [[3:17|Be ye followers of me, brethren|Imitatores mei estote, o fratres]], that is, conform yourselves to me in the virtues set out above, and in every virtuous work, [[3:17|and observe|et observate]], that is, attend carefully and take care to follow, […] [[3:17|you have our model|habetis formam nostram]] [the lost words are presumably the lemma eos qui ita ambulant, sicut, them who walk so as], that is, virtuous men who live in such a way as I have shown you, by word and deed, that one ought to live. But beware of the others. For [[Matt 7:16|By their fruits you shall know|A fructibus enim eorum cognoscetis]] whether they live according to the pattern of our life and are worthy of imitation [the margin gives Matth. xvi, 16; the words are Matt 7:16, and again 7:20].

paras.t: Multi enim ambulant per vitiorum abrupta, et vias perversas de quibus Salomon : Via, inquit, impiorum tenebrosa, nesciunt ubi corruunt. Qui et in die judicii dicent illud Sapientiæ : Lassati sumus in via iniquitatis et perditionis, et ambulavimus vias difficiles. De quibus ait Christus : Lata et spatiosa est via quæ ducit ad mortem, et multi vadunt per eam. Quos sæpe dicebam vobis, dum eram vobiscum (nunc autem et flens ex compassione eorum et dolore, quia tot fallunt, dico, id est, nomino eos), inimicos crucis Christi, id est Christi crucifixi, quoniam contra ejus doctrinam et jussa, legalia prædicant et vitiis subjacent.
paras.en: [[3:18|For many walk|Multi enim ambulant]] over the precipices of vices, and in the perverse ways of which Solomon says: [[Prov 4:19|The way|Via]], he says, [[Prov 4:19|of the wicked is darksome: they know not where they fall|impiorum tenebrosa, nesciunt ubi corruunt]]. And these at the day of judgement will say that word of Wisdom: [[Wis 5:7|We wearied ourselves in the way of iniquity and destruction, and have walked through hard ways|Lassati sumus in via iniquitatis et perditionis, et ambulavimus vias difficiles]]. Of them Christ says: [[Matt 7:13|broad is the way that leadeth to destruction, and many there are who go in thereat|Lata et spatiosa est via quæ ducit ad mortem, et multi vadunt per eam]] [the margin gives Matth. xii, 13; the passage is Matt 7:13, which Denis quotes freely: broad and spacious is the way that leadeth to death, and many go by it]. [[3:18|of whom I have told you often|Quos sæpe dicebam vobis]], while I was with you ([[3:18|and now tell you weeping|nunc autem et flens]] out of compassion for them and out of grief, because so many are deceived, I [[3:18|tell|dico]], that is, I name them), [[3:18|that they are enemies of the cross of Christ|inimicos crucis Christi]], that is, of Christ crucified, since against his teaching and commands they preach the legal observances and lie subject to vices.

paras.t: Quorum finis, id est mors, erit interitus, id est ingressus seu via æternæ damnationis, quam statim quum moriuntur, incurrunt. Quorum deus venter est, id est, delectationibus gulæ ita insistunt quasi in repletione ventris salus consisteret. Unde ventrem suum plus colunt quam Deum. Quod autem quis maxime colit, hoc deus ejus asseritur. De quibus Judas in sua testatur Canonica : Hi sunt in epulis convivantes sine timore, semetipsos pascentes, quibus procella tenebrarum conservata est usque in æternum. Et gloria horum vana, qua in vitiis istis, vel in cærimonialibus legis exsultant, erit in confusione ipsorum, id est, confusibilis erit eis et inhonesta coram divino judicio : unde per Prophetam Dominus protestatur, Gloriam eorum in ignominiam commutabo ; qui terrena sapiunt, id est, in carnalibus potius quam in spiritualibus delectantur.
paras.en: [[3:19|Whose end|Quorum finis]], that is, death, will be [[3:19|destruction|interitus]], that is, the entrance or way into eternal damnation, which they incur the moment they die; [[3:19|whose God is their belly|Quorum deus venter est]], that is, they give themselves to the pleasures of gluttony as though salvation lay in filling the belly. Hence they worship their belly more than God. For what a man worships most is said to be his god. Of these Jude testifies in his Canonical Epistle: [[Jude 1:12|These are spots in their banquets, feasting together without fear, feeding themselves|Hi sunt in epulis convivantes sine timore, semetipsos pascentes]] [Denis's wording leaves out maculæ, spots], [[Jude 1:13|to whom the storm of darkness is reserved for ever|quibus procella tenebrarum conservata est usque in æternum]]. [[3:19|and whose glory|Et gloria horum]], that vain glory in which they exult in these vices or in the ceremonies of the law, will be [[3:19|in their shame|in confusione ipsorum]], that is, it will bring them shame and disgrace before the divine judgement: hence the Lord protests through the Prophet, [[Osee 4:7|I will change their glory into shame|Gloriam eorum in ignominiam commutabo]] [the margin gives Osee v, 7; the words are Osee 4:7]; [[3:19|who mind earthly things|qui terrena sapiunt]], that is, they delight in carnal rather than in spiritual things.

paras.t: Nostra autem conversatio in cœlis est, per contemplationem et desiderium bonorum cœlestium. Nunc enim nostra conversatio in cœlis est per spem, jugem intentionem, et ratione objecti seu termini motus, quod est in cœlo, videlicet Deus et æterna felicitas. Anima namque, secundum Augustinum, verius est ubi amat, quam ubi animat. Denique, Ubi thesaurus tuus, ibi et cor tuum. Eorum itaque conversatio est in cœlis; qui omnia temporalia atque carnalia transcendentes, cœliformem et angelicam vitam ducunt in terra, illi uni quod solum necessarium est, tota mente intenti. Unde etiam Salvatorem expectamus cum magna securitate, videlicet Dominum nostrum Jesum Christum venturum ad universale judicium. Qui enim in cœlis conversationem jam habent, quamvis adhuc viatores sint, secure præstolantur Christi adventum.
paras.en: [[3:20|But our conversation is in heaven|Nostra autem conversatio in cœlis est]] [conversatio: our way of life, our dwelling as citizens], by contemplation and desire of heavenly goods. For even now our conversation is in heaven by hope and constant intention, and by reason of the object or term of our movement, which is in heaven, namely God and eternal happiness. For the soul, according to Augustine, is more truly where it loves than where it gives life [ubi amat … ubi animat: where it loves … where it animates]. And finally: [[Matt 6:21|where thy treasure is, there is thy heart also|Ubi thesaurus tuus, ibi et cor tuum]]. Their conversation, therefore, is in heaven who, passing beyond all temporal and carnal things, lead a heavenly and angelic life on earth, intent with their whole mind on that one thing which alone is necessary[[Luke 10:42||]]. [[3:20|from whence also we look for the Saviour|Unde etiam Salvatorem expectamus]] with great security, namely [[3:20|our Lord Jesus Christ|Dominum nostrum Jesum Christum]], who will come to the universal judgement. For those who already have their conversation in heaven, though they are still wayfarers, await Christ's coming securely.

paras.t: Qui reformabit, id est, ad pristinam formam reducet ac suscitabit in die judicii, corpus humilitatis nostræ, id est corpus istud passibile, in quo dejectionem tribulationemque patimur : quod etiam nobis occasio est ad humiliandum nos ipsos, pensantes quod pulvis sumus. Sic autem reformabit illud, quod erit configuratum corpori claritatis suæ, id est, simile erit corpori Christi glorificato. In tali etenim corpore Sancti resurgent. Sic igitur faciet Christus secundum operationem, id est virtutem operativam, qua possit etiam subjicere sibi omnia, id est de singulis ordinare et facere quod sibi placuerit, hoc est secundum divinam potentiam, per quam reformatio ista complebitur. Subest enim Deo, quum voluerit, posse, ut dicit Sapiens.
paras.en: [[3:21|Who will reform|Qui reformabit]], that is, will bring back to its former shape and raise up at the day of judgement, [[3:21|the body of our lowness|corpus humilitatis nostræ]], that is, this passible body [that is, one able to suffer], in which we suffer abasement and tribulation: which is also an occasion for us to humble ourselves, considering that we are dust[[Gen 3:19||]]. And he will so reform it that it will be [[3:21|made like to the body of his glory|configuratum corpori claritatis suæ]], that is, it will be like the glorified body of Christ. For in such a body the Saints will rise. Thus, then, Christ will do this [[3:21|according to the operation|secundum operationem]], that is, the working power, [[3:21|whereby also he is able to subdue all things unto himself|qua possit etiam subjicere sibi omnia]], that is, to order each thing and do with it what pleases him: that is, according to the divine power, by which this reforming will be accomplished. For, as the Wise Man says, [[Wis 12:18|thy power is at hand when thou wilt|Subest enim Deo, quum voluerit, posse]] [Denis has Deo, to God, where the Wise Man, speaking to God, has tibi, to thee].

4.title: EXPOSITIO CAPITULI QUARTI : ITAQUE, FRATRES MEI CARISSIMI, ETC.
4.title_en: Exposition of the fourth chapter: Therefore, my dearly beloved brethren, etc.

paras.t: Consequenter, post exhortationes præhabitas consolatur Apostolus Philippenses. Itaque, id est, quoniam tantam beatitudinem exspectamus et sortituri sumus, o fratres mei carissimi, secundum appetitum superiorem seu intellectualem, id est valde dilecti, quoad futuram felicitatem in patria, et desideratissimi, secundum appetitum inferiorem ac sensitivum, ordinatum et rationi subjectum, id est valde a me desiderati, quoad mutuum conspectum in hac vita : propono enim venire ad vos; gaudium meum materialiter, id est, de quorum profectu et gratia gaudeo, et corona mea, id est augmentum gloriæ meæ in patria, quoniam omnium meritorum vestrorum sum particeps tanquam institutor vester ac doctor ; sic state in Domino, carissimi, id est, constantes atque immobiles estote in Deo, adhærendo justitiæ sicut et ego, ut dicere valeatis illud Job : Justificationem quam cœpi tenere, non deseram.
paras.en: Next, after the exhortations already given, the Apostle consoles the Philippians. [[4:1|Therefore|Itaque]], that is, since we await so great a beatitude and are to obtain it, O [[4:1|my dearly beloved brethren|fratres mei carissimi]], according to the higher or intellectual appetite, that is, greatly loved, as regards the future happiness in the fatherland, [[4:1|and most desired|et desideratissimi]], according to the lower and sensitive appetite, ordered and subject to reason, that is, greatly desired by me, as regards seeing one another in this life: for I purpose to come to you; [[4:1|my joy|gaudium meum]] materially [that is, as the matter or occasion of my joy], that is, you at whose progress and grace I rejoice, [[4:1|and my crown|et corona mea]], that is, the increase of my glory in the fatherland, since I share in all your merits as your founder and teacher; [[4:1|so stand fast in the Lord, my dearly beloved|sic state in Domino, carissimi]], that is, be constant and immovable in God, cleaving to justice as I do, so that you may say that word of Job: [[Job 27:6|My justification, which I have begun to hold, I will not forsake|Justificationem quam cœpi tenere, non deseram]].

paras.t: Evodiam rogo et Syntychen deprecor id ipsum sapere, id est idem sentire cum aliis sanctis. in Domino. Has duas devotas matronas exprimit nominatim, quia spectabilis erant vitæ, et fidelibus necessaria ministraverunt.
paras.en: [[4:2|I beg of Evodia and I beseech Syntyche to be of one mind|Evodiam rogo et Syntychen deprecor id ipsum sapere]], that is, to think the same as the other saints, [[4:2|in the Lord|in Domino]]. He names these two devout matrons expressly, because they were of notable life and ministered necessaries to the faithful.

paras.t: Etiam rogo et te, Germane compar, id est, adjutor et socius meus. Est autem Germanus nomen proprium viri, qui inter Philippenses egregius fuit. Adjuva illas, id est, prælatas feminas conforta in bono, quæ mecum laboraverunt in Evangelio, id est in prædicatione evangelicæ veritatis : non utique prædicando, quoniam mulierem docere non permitto, sed mihi evangelizanti necessaria ministrando ; cum Clemente, id est etiam Clementi, et ceteris adjutoribus meis collaboraverunt, ministrando necessaria eis, sicut et mihi ; quorum nomina scripta sunt in libro vitæ, id est, qui ad æternam beatitudinem præordinati sunt, ut confido, vel, ut ex divina revelatione certo scio. Porro, secundum Thomam in prima parte, liber vitæ in Deo metaphorice dicitur. Quemadmodum enim homo eos conscribit qui ad se specialiter pertinent, sic dicitur Deus scripsisse electos qui ad eum finaliter spectant. Unde ipsa electorum conscriptio in mente divina, seu firma eorum notitia in intellectu divino, liber vitæ vocatur, qui aliud prorsus non est nisi prædestinatio Dei. Quum autem dicitur liber vitæ, intelligendum est de vita gloriæ. De hoc libro ait Salvator : Gaudete quod nomina vestra scripta sunt in libro vitæ. Quod vero prædicti scripti fuerint in libro vitæ, Paulus certo scire non potuit nisi per revelationem divinam.
paras.en: [[4:3|And I entreat thee also, my sincere companion|Etiam rogo et te, Germane compar]], that is, my helper and comrade. Now Germanus is the proper name of a man who was eminent among the Philippians [Denis takes *germane*, “genuine”, as a proper name]. [[4:3|help those women|Adjuva illas]], that is, strengthen in good the women aforesaid, [[4:3|who have laboured with me in the gospel|quæ mecum laboraverunt in Evangelio]], that is, in the preaching of the gospel truth: not indeed by preaching, since I suffer not a woman to teach[[1 Tim 2:12||]], but by ministering necessaries to me as I preached the gospel; [[4:3|with Clement|cum Clemente]], that is, they laboured also with Clement [[4:3|and the rest of my fellow labourers|et ceteris adjutoribus meis]], ministering necessaries to them as to me; [[4:3|whose names are in the book of life|quorum nomina scripta sunt in libro vitæ]] (Denis reads “are written”), that is, who have been foreordained to eternal beatitude, as I trust, or as I know for certain from divine revelation. Moreover, according to Thomas in the First Part, the book of life is said of God metaphorically. For as a man enrols those who belong to him in a special way, so God is said to have written the elect, who are ordered to him as their end. Hence this enrolment of the elect in the divine mind, or the firm knowledge of them in the divine intellect, is called the book of life, which is nothing else at all than the predestination of God. And when it is called the book of life, it is to be understood of the life of glory. Of this book the Saviour says: Rejoice [[Luke 10:20|that your names are written in heaven|quod nomina vestra scripta sunt]] in the book of life [the margin gives “cf. Luke x, 20”; the Gospel has “in heaven”]. But that the aforesaid were written in the book of life, Paul could not know for certain except by divine revelation.

paras.t: Præterea admonet Apostolus Philippenses ad spiritualem ac jugem lætitiam. Gaudete in Domino semper, id est, in Deo tanquam in objecto, videlicet in contemplatione et dilectione Dei beneficiorumque ejus, imo in omni eo quod Domino placet, spiritualiter exsultate, divinæ perfectioni, majestati ac beatitudini cordialiter congaudendo, de beneficiis quoque ejus nobis collatis sive promissis lætando, et in omni actu virtuoso quo Deus honoratur et colitur, delectando. Signum namque virtutis, est delectatio operis, secundum Philosophum. Semper autem gaudendum est hoc modo, actu vel habitu, seu debitis horis, vel in prosperis et adversis, sicut alibi dicit Apostolus : Quasi tristes, semper autem gaudentes. Sed gaudium istud, durante præsentis peregrinationis exsilio, non excludit admixtionem omnis tristitiæ. Hoc gaudium fuit in Virgine gloriosa, quæ cecinit : Exsultavit spiritus meus in Deo salutari meo. Non ergo in creaturis gaudendum est, nisi per relationem ad Deum, in quantum earum usus, amor, possessio, vel notitia manuducit ad Deum. Iterum dico, ad excitandum vestræ devotionis affectum, et meæ exhortationis veritatem confirmandum, gaudete in Domino, modo præfato, servientes ei hilariter, imo cum jubilo cordis.
paras.en: Further, the Apostle urges the Philippians to spiritual and constant gladness. [[4:4|Rejoice in the Lord always|Gaudete in Domino semper]], that is, exult spiritually in God as in your object, namely in the contemplation and love of God and of his benefits, nay in everything that pleases the Lord: rejoicing from the heart with the divine perfection, majesty and beatitude, being glad also at his benefits bestowed on us or promised, and taking delight in every virtuous act by which God is honoured and worshipped. For the sign of virtue is delight in the work, according to the Philosopher [Aristotle]. And one must always rejoice in this way, in act or in habit, or at due hours, or in prosperity and adversity, as the Apostle says elsewhere: [[2 Cor 6:10|As sorrowful, yet always rejoicing|Quasi tristes, semper autem gaudentes]]. But this joy, while the exile of the present pilgrimage lasts, does not exclude the admixture of every sadness. This joy was in the glorious Virgin, who sang: [[Luke 1:47|And my spirit hath rejoiced in God my Saviour|Exsultavit spiritus meus in Deo salutari meo]]. One must not, therefore, rejoice in creatures except by reference to God, in so far as their use, love, possession or knowledge leads us by the hand to God. [[4:4|again, I say|Iterum dico]], to stir up the affection of your devotion and to confirm the truth of my exhortation, [[4:4|rejoice|gaudete]] in the Lord in the manner said, serving him cheerfully, nay with jubilation of heart.

paras.t: Modestia vestra in verbis et factis, id est conversationis vestræ moderatio, discretio, ordinatusque modus, nota sit omnibus hominibus, id est, talis ac tanta sit, ut omnibus innotescat per visum vel famam, ad gloriam Creatoris, et proximorum ædificationem, sicut in Evangelio Dominus loquitur : Sic luceat lux vestra coram hominibus, etc. Dominus prope est, id est paratus ad succurrendum : imo per pietatem et gratiam suam in vobis habitat. Unde et ipse testatur : Deliciæ meæ esse cum filiis hominum. Et rursus : Ego sto ad ostium et pulso ; si quis aperuerit mihi januam, intrabo ad illum et cœnabo cum eo. In omnibus quoque est Deus per essentiam, præsentiam atque potentiam. In ipso etiam vivimus, movemur et sumus. Denique, prope est Deus orantibus et afflictis, juxta illud : Prope est Dominus omnibus invocantibus eum ; et, Cum ipso sum in tribulatione. Intus est diligentibus, sicut ait Joannes : Qui manet in caritate, in Deo manet, et Deus in eo. Longe est ab impiis, prout in Proverbiis legitur. Propter quod per Jeremiam dicit : Non est anima mea ad populum istum.
paras.en: [[4:5|Let your modesty|Modestia vestra]] in words and deeds, that is, the moderation, discretion and ordered measure of your conduct, [[4:5|be known to all men|nota sit omnibus hominibus]], that is, be such and so great that it becomes known to all by sight or report, to the glory of the Creator and the edification of your neighbours, as the Lord says in the Gospel: [[Matt 5:16|So let your light shine before men|Sic luceat lux vestra coram hominibus]], etc. [[4:5|The Lord is nigh|Dominus prope est]], that is, ready to help: nay, by his kindness and grace he dwells in you. Hence he himself testifies: [[Prov 8:31|my delights were to be with the children of men|Deliciæ meæ esse cum filiis hominum]]. And again: [[Apoc 3:20|Behold, I stand at the gate and knock. If any man shall hear my voice and open to me the door, I will come in to him and will sup with him|Ego sto ad ostium et pulso ; si quis aperuerit mihi januam, intrabo ad illum et cœnabo cum eo]]. God is also in all things by essence, presence and power. In him too we live, and move, and are[[Acts 17:28||]]. Lastly, God is near to those who pray and those afflicted, according to that: [[Ps 144:18|The Lord is nigh unto all them that call upon him|Prope est Dominus omnibus invocantibus eum]]; and, [[Ps 90:15|I am with him in tribulation|Cum ipso sum in tribulatione]]. He is within those who love him, as John says: [[1 John 4:16|he that abideth in charity abideth in God, and God in him|Qui manet in caritate, in Deo manet, et Deus in eo]]. He is far from the wicked, as we read in Proverbs[[Prov 15:29||]]. Wherefore he says through Jeremias: [[Jer 15:1|my soul is not towards this people|Non est anima mea ad populum istum]].

paras.t: Nihil solliciti sitis : id est, quum Dominus prope sit, de nulla re angustiari, seu inordinatam curam habere debetis ; sed primo quærite regnum Dei, et omnia necessaria adjicientur vobis. Unde et Petrus : Omnem, inquit, sollicitudinem vestram projicientes in Deum, quoniam ipsi cura est de vobis ; et Christus, Nolite solliciti esse in crastinum. Omnia hæc de inordinata atque superflua cura, quæ ad diffidentiam quodammodo pertinet, asseruntur : de qua Salomon dicit, Spes sollicitorum peribit. Verumtamen, sicut frequenter præhabitum est, est quædam sollicitudo spiritualis ac ordinata, quæ est diligens animi vigilantia circa bona honesta aut necessaria : quam sæpe commendat præcipitque Scriptura, ut est istud, Custodi temetipsum et animam tuam sollicite ; item, Solliciti servare unitatem spiritus in vinculo pacis.
paras.en: [[4:6|Be nothing solicitous|Nihil solliciti sitis]]: that is, since the Lord is nigh, you ought to be anxious about nothing, or to have inordinate care; but [[Matt 6:33|Seek ye therefore first the kingdom of God, and his justice, and all these things shall be added unto you|primo quærite regnum Dei, et omnia necessaria adjicientur vobis]] (all necessary things, says Denis). Hence Peter too says: [[1 Pet 5:7|Casting all your care upon him, for he hath care of you|Omnem … sollicitudinem vestram … cura est de vobis]]; and Christ: [[Matt 6:34|Be not therefore solicitous for to morrow|Nolite solliciti esse in crastinum]]. All these things are said of inordinate and superfluous care, which belongs in a way to distrust: of which Solomon says: [[Prov 11:7|the expectation of the solicitous shall perish|Spes sollicitorum peribit]]. Yet, as has often been said before, there is a certain spiritual and ordered solicitude, which is a diligent watchfulness of mind about goods that are honourable or necessary: this Scripture often commends and commands, as in this: [[Deut 4:9|Keep thyself therefore, and thy soul carefully|Custodi temetipsum et animam tuam sollicite]]; and again: [[Eph 4:3|Careful to keep the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace|Solliciti servare unitatem spiritus in vinculo pacis]].

paras.t: Sed in omni oratione et obsecratione cum gratiarum actione, petitiones vestræ innotescant apud Deum. Hic ponuntur quatuor partes orationis vel species, quarum distinctio est. Oratio enim est simplex precatio, quæ est de facilioribus impetrandis. Obsecratio est invocatio Dei cum commemoratione sacrorum seu divinorum, quorum virtute aut merito aliquid impetrare optamus : sicut quum dicimus, Per passionem tuam, vel, Propter bonitatem tuam, exaudi nos. Estque obsecratio pro difficilioribus obtinendis, ut est justificatio impii. Petitio vero est invocatio Dei pro bonis gratiæ, quæ ordinantur ad bona gloriæ. Alibi quoque ponit Apostolus aliud genus orationis, quod dicitur postulatio, quæ est pro bonis patriæ. Sæpius tamen unum istorum pro alio sumitur. Hortatur ergo Apostolus, ut petitiones nostræ factæ in omni, id est quacumque, oratione et obsecratione et gratiarum actione, ex tanta puritate, attentione et fervore mentis procedant, quatenus apud Deum innotescant, id est a Deo attendantur, et per acceptationem noscantur, atque ab angelis sanctis ei præsententur, quemadmodum in Actibus angelus ait Cornelio : Orationes tuæ et eleemosynæ ascenderunt in memoriam in conspectu Dei. Et in Paralipomenon libro scriptum est, quod Isaias et Ezechias vociferati sunt usque in cœlum contra Sennacherib, pervenitque oratio eorum ad habitaculum sanctum Dei.
paras.en: [[4:6|but in every thing, by prayer and supplication, with thanksgiving, let your petitions be made known to God|Sed in omni oratione et obsecratione cum gratiarum actione, petitiones vestræ innotescant apud Deum]]. Here four parts or kinds of prayer are set down, between which there is a distinction. For *prayer* is simple entreaty, which concerns obtaining easier things. *Supplication* [Latin *obsecratio*, from *ob sacra*, “by holy things”] is the invocation of God with mention of sacred or divine things by whose power or merit we desire to obtain something: as when we say, By thy passion, or, For thy goodness' sake, hear us. And supplication is for obtaining more difficult things, such as the justification of the ungodly. *Petition* is the invocation of God for the goods of grace, which are ordered to the goods of glory. Elsewhere the Apostle sets down another kind of prayer too, called *postulation*[[1 Tim 2:1||]], which is for the goods of the fatherland. Yet more often one of these is taken for another. The Apostle therefore exhorts that our petitions, made in every, that is, any, prayer and supplication and thanksgiving, should proceed from such purity, attention and fervour of mind that they may be known to God, that is, heeded by God and known by being accepted, and presented to him by the holy angels, as in the Acts the angel says to Cornelius: [[Acts 10:4|Thy prayers and thy alms are ascended for a memorial in the sight of God|Orationes tuæ et eleemosynæ ascenderunt in memoriam in conspectu Dei]]. And in the book of Paralipomenon it is written that Isaias and Ezechias cried out even to heaven against Sennacherib[[2 Par 32:20||]], and their prayer came to the holy dwelling place of God[[2 Par 30:27||]].

paras.t: Et pax Dei increata, immensa, æterna, id est Deus pacificus, quæ pax exsuperat omnem sensum, id est, omnem intellectum creatum, angelicum et humanum, omnemque gustum et experientiam ejus in infinitum excedit, custodiat effective corda vestra, id est voluntates ab omni prava affectione, et intelligentias vestras, id est intellectum speculativum et practicum omnium vestrum, ab omni errore, in Christo Jesu, id est per gratiam et meritum Christi; vel, In Christo Jesu, id est, ut jugiter maneatis in ipso. Vel sic: Pax Dei creata, videlicet tranquillitas mentis a Deo infusa, quæ exsuperat omnem sensum, quoad suam fontalem plenitudinem seu plenam perfectionem; vel, Exsuperat omnem sensum viatorum, secundum quod in patria habetur ac degustatur; custodiat formaliter corda vestra et intelligentias a perturbatione et inquietudine, quatenus pax ista in vobis permaneat, et vitia sibi opposita ab interioribus vestris excludat.
paras.en: [[4:7|And the peace of God|Et pax Dei]], uncreated, immense, eternal, that is, God the peacemaker, [[4:7|which surpasseth all understanding|quæ exsuperat omnem sensum]], that is, which infinitely exceeds every created intellect, angelic and human, and all its taste and experience, [[4:7|keep your hearts|custodiat corda vestra]] effectively [that is, as the efficient cause], that is, your wills from every evil affection, [[4:7|and minds|et intelligentias vestras]], that is, the speculative and practical intellect of all of you, from every error, [[4:7|in Christ Jesus|in Christo Jesu]], that is, through the grace and merit of Christ; or, in Christ Jesus, that is, so that you may abide in him continually. Or thus: the created peace of God, namely tranquillity of mind infused by God, which surpasses all understanding as to its fontal fulness or full perfection; or, surpasses all the understanding of wayfarers, as it is possessed and tasted in the fatherland; keep formally [that is, as the form in the soul itself] your hearts and minds from disturbance and disquiet, so that this peace may abide in you and shut out from your inner parts the vices opposed to it.

paras.t: De cetero, fratres, quæcumque sunt vera veritate doctrinæ, vitæ aut justitiæ, quæcumque pudica, id est verba et facta casta, lasciviam excludentia, quæcumque sunt justa quoad proximum, quæcumque sancta quantum ad cultum divinum, quæcumque amabilia, id est, quæ inducunt ad mutuam amicitiam, quæcumque bonæ famæ, id est, quæ bonam famam pariunt et conservant, si qua virtus, id est, quia est aliqua virtus moralis, intellectualis et theologicalis vobis necessaria, si qua laus disciplinæ, id est, quia est aliqua disciplina morum, laudabilis scilicet compositio motuum ac sensuum exteriorum; hæc cogitate assidue, non solum ut sciatis, sed ut ea agendo seu obtinendo, virtuosi salvique sitis, quæ et didicistis ex mea prædicatione, et accepistis per cognitionem intellectivam, et audistis, id est, ab aliis percepistis ea esse in me, et vidistis per experientiam hoc verum esse. Hæc opera virtuosa agite, et Deus dator, amator et conservator pacis internæ, erit vobiscum quotidie per gratiam ampliorem.
paras.en: [[4:8|For the rest, brethren, whatsoever things are true|De cetero, fratres, quæcumque sunt vera]] with the truth of doctrine, of life or of justice, [[4:8|whatsoever modest|quæcumque pudica]], that is, chaste words and deeds that shut out wantonness, [[4:8|whatsoever just|quæcumque justa]] as regards one's neighbour, [[4:8|whatsoever holy|quæcumque sancta]] as regards divine worship, [[4:8|whatsoever lovely|quæcumque amabilia]], that is, things that lead to mutual friendship, [[4:8|whatsoever of good fame|quæcumque bonæ famæ]], that is, things that beget and preserve a good name, [[4:8|if there be any virtue|si qua virtus]], that is, since there is some virtue, moral, intellectual and theological, necessary to you, [[4:8|if any praise of discipline|si qua laus disciplinæ]], that is, since there is a certain discipline of manners, namely a praiseworthy ordering of the outward movements and senses; [[4:8|think on these things|hæc cogitate]] assiduously, not only that you may know them, but that by doing or attaining them you may be virtuous and saved; [[4:9|The things which you have both learned|quæ et didicistis]] from my preaching, [[4:9|and received|et accepistis]] by intellectual knowledge, [[4:9|and heard|et audistis]], that is, learned from others to be [[4:9|in me|in me]], [[4:9|and seen|et vidistis]] by experience to be true: [[4:9|these do ye|Hæc agite]] as virtuous works, [[4:9|and the God of peace shall be with you|et Deus pacis erit vobiscum]]: God, the giver, lover and preserver of inward peace, will be with you daily by more abundant grace.

paras.t: Insuper congratulatur Apostolus liberalitati Philippensium, non principaliter ob proprium emolumentum, sed propter illorum caritatem ac meritum. Gavisus sum autem in Domino vehementer, quoniam tandem aliquando, id est post tempora longa, refloruistis, id est, more arboris iterum floruistis, seu fructuose viguistis et convaluistis, pro me sentire, et meæ inopiæ compati atque succurrere, sicut et ante sentiebatis pro me. Occupati autem eratis negotiis aliis : idcirco excusabiles estis de tanta dilatione refloritionis istius.
paras.en: Moreover the Apostle congratulates the Philippians on their liberality, not chiefly for his own profit, but because of their charity and merit. [[4:10|Now I rejoice in the Lord exceedingly that now at length|Gavisus sum autem in Domino vehementer, quoniam tandem aliquando]], that is, after a long time, [[4:10|your thought for me hath flourished again|refloruistis pro me sentire]], that is, you have blossomed again like a tree, or thrived and grown strong fruitfully, in thinking for me, and in sympathizing with and relieving my need, [[4:10|as you did also think|sicut et sentiebatis]] for me before. [[4:10|but you were busied|Occupati autem eratis]] with other affairs: therefore you are excusable for so long a delay in this reflowering.

paras.t: Non quasi propter penuriam dico, id est, non ex necessitudine paupertatis meæ hæc assero, ut sustentetur a vobis. Ego enim didici, per gratiam Dei et consuetudinem exercitii mei, in quibus sum, sufficiens esse, id est, quid mihi sufficiat. Natura quippe paucis minimisque contenta est. Scio et humiliari, id est actum humilitatis, tribulationis seu paupertatis prompte et discrete exsequi, scio et abundare, id est in abundantia temporalium non excedere (ubique et in omnibus exercitiis virtutum institutus, id est bene instructus, sum): sciens videlicet et satiari sine immoderantia, et esurire sine impatientia, et abundare, non tamen cor rebus caducis apponere, et penuriam pati in victu ac vestibus sine tristitia. Omnia hæc possum, non propriis viribus, sed in eo qui me confortat, id est per adjutorium Christi. Verumtamen bene fecistis: id est, quamvis donis vestris possem carere, tamen bene et caritative egistis, communicantes, id est eleemosynam vestram impertientes, tribulationi meæ, id est mihi incarcerato atque afflicto.
paras.en: [[4:11|I speak not as it were for want|Non quasi propter penuriam dico]], that is, I do not say this out of the need of my poverty, that I may be supported by you. [[4:11|For I have learned|Ego enim didici]], by the grace of God and the custom of my practice, [[4:11|in whatsoever state I am, to be content therewith|in quibus sum, sufficiens esse]], that is, what suffices me. For nature is content with few and very small things. [[4:12|I know both how to be brought low|Scio et humiliari]], that is, to carry out promptly and discreetly the act of humility, of tribulation or of poverty, [[4:12|and I know how to abound|scio et abundare]], that is, not to go to excess in an abundance of temporal things [[4:12|(every where and in all things I am instructed)|(ubique et in omnibus institutus sum)]] in the exercises of the virtues, that is, well taught: knowing, namely, [[4:12|both to be full|et satiari]] without immoderation, [[4:12|and to be hungry|et esurire]] without impatience, [[4:12|both to abound|et abundare]] yet not set the heart on perishable things, [[4:12|and to suffer need|et penuriam pati]] in food and clothing without sadness. [[4:13|I can do all things|Omnia possum]], not by my own strength, but [[4:13|in him who strengtheneth me|in eo qui me confortat]], that is, by the help of Christ. [[4:14|Nevertheless, you have done well|Verumtamen bene fecistis]]: that is, though I could do without your gifts, yet you have acted well and charitably, [[4:14|in communicating|communicantes]], that is, imparting your alms, [[4:14|to my tribulation|tribulationi meæ]], that is, to me imprisoned and afflicted.

paras.t: Præterea præfert Apostolus Philippenses aliis, quantum ad aliquid, quatenus laudibus suis auditis, provocentur ad meliora. Virtus enim laudata, augetur in bonis. Scitis autem et vos, Philippenses, quod in principio Evangelii, id est illo tempore prædicationis meæ evangelicæ, quando profectus sum, id est recessi, a Macedonia, verbo prædicationis illic disseminato, nulla mihi ecclesia communicavit, id est, temporalia dedit, in ratione dati et accepti, id est in rationabili recompensatione temporalium, pro exhibitione spiritualium quæ vobis communicavi : rationis enim censura hoc dictat, ut spiritualia bona præstanti seu dispensanti, temporalia ministrentur ; nisi vos soli : in quo declaratur gratitudo ac liberalitas vestra ; quia et Thessalonicam, id est ad urbem sic dictam, semel et bis, id est tribus vicibus, vel semel et iterum, in usum, id est ad utendum, mihi misistis temporalia vestra, ut necessaria vitæ ex eis acciperem. Non quia quæro datum, id est, non ideo vos commendo quia munera vestra requiro, sed requiro fructum abundantem, id est meritum copiosum, in ratione vestra jam dicta, videlicet in rationabili recompensatione qua mihi temporalia pro spiritualibus communicatis. Habeo autem omnia quæ misistis, et abundo in eis, ita ut aliis indigentibus ea communicem. Repletus sum gaudio mentis et copia rerum, acceptis ab Epaphrodito his quæ misistis mihi, odorem suavitatis, id est, quæ sic placent Deo ut odor suavissimus. Eleemosyna namque est hostia Deo gratissima. Ideo sequitur : hostiam acceptam, Deo placentem. Unde ad Hebræos ait : Beneficentiæ et communionis nolite oblivisci : talibus enim hostiis placatur Deus.
paras.en: Further, the Apostle sets the Philippians above others in a certain respect, so that, hearing their own praises, they may be stirred to better things. For virtue praised grows in the good. [[4:15|And you also know, O Philippians, that in the beginning of the gospel|Scitis autem et vos, Philippenses, quod in principio Evangelii]], that is, at that time of my gospel preaching, [[4:15|when I departed|quando profectus sum]], that is, withdrew, [[4:15|from Macedonia|a Macedonia]], the word of preaching having been sown there, [[4:15|no church communicated with me|nulla mihi ecclesia communicavit]], that is, gave temporal things, [[4:15|as concerning giving and receiving|in ratione dati et accepti]], that is, in reasonable recompense of temporal things for the spiritual things I imparted to you: for the judgment of reason dictates this, that temporal things be ministered to him who furnishes or dispenses spiritual goods[[1 Cor 9:11||]][[Rom 15:27||]] [the margin gives 1 Cor ix, 11–13 and Rom xv, 27]; [[4:15|but you only|nisi vos soli]]: in which your gratitude and liberality are shown; [[4:16|For unto Thessalonica also|quia et Thessalonicam]], that is, to the city so called, [[4:16|you sent once and again|semel et bis]], that is, three times, or once and a second time, [[4:16|for my use|in usum]], that is, to be used, your temporal goods, that I might take from them the necessaries of life. [[4:17|Not that I seek the gift|Non quia quæro datum]], that is, I do not commend you because I seek your gifts, [[4:17|but I seek the fruit that may abound|sed requiro fructum abundantem]], that is, copious merit, [[4:17|to your account|in ratione vestra]] already mentioned, namely in the reasonable recompense by which you impart to me temporal things for spiritual. [[4:18|But I have all|Habeo autem omnia]] that you sent, [[4:18|and abound|et abundo]] in them, so that I share them with others in need. [[4:18|I am filled|Repletus sum]] with joy of mind and plenty of things, [[4:18|having received from Epaphroditus the things you sent|acceptis ab Epaphrodito his quæ misistis]] me, [[4:18|an odour of sweetness|odorem suavitatis]], that is, things which so please God as a most sweet odour. For alms is a sacrifice most pleasing to God. Therefore it follows: [[4:18|an acceptable sacrifice, pleasing to God|hostiam acceptam, placentem Deo]]. Hence he says to the Hebrews: [[Heb 13:16|And do not forget to do good and to impart: for by such sacrifices God's favour is obtained|Beneficentiæ et communionis nolite oblivisci : talibus enim hostiis placatur Deus]].

paras.t: Deus autem meus impleat, id est, exaudiat et operi mancipet, omne desiderium vestrum rationabile et sincerum, secundum divitias suas in gloria, id est pie, gratiose et copiose, secundum quod ipse in se dives est in gloria, id est in beatitudine sua. Vel, Impleat desiderium vestrum in gloria, dando videlicet vobis gloriam sempiternam; in Christo Jesu, id est per Dominum Salvatorem, et per gratiam seu meritum ejus. Deo autem per creationem, et Patri nostro per gubernationem, videlicet summæ et incommutabili Trinitati, sit gloria in sæcula sæculorum. Amen.
paras.en: [[4:19|And may my God supply|Deus autem meus impleat]], that is, hear and bring to effect, [[4:19|all your want|omne desiderium vestrum]] [Latin *desiderium*, “desire”], reasonable and sincere, [[4:19|according to his riches in glory|secundum divitias suas in gloria]], that is, kindly, graciously and abundantly, according as he is himself rich in glory, that is, in his beatitude. Or, may he fulfil your desire in glory, namely by giving you everlasting glory; [[4:19|in Christ Jesus|in Christo Jesu]], that is, through the Lord the Saviour, and through his grace or merit. [[4:20|Now to God|Deo autem]] by creation, [[4:20|and our Father|et Patri nostro]] by governance, namely to the supreme and unchangeable Trinity, be [[4:20|glory, world without end. Amen|gloria in sæcula sæculorum. Amen]].

paras.t: Salutate, id est, salutem optate ac dicite, omnes sanctos ad vestram societatem spectantes, in Christo Jesu, id est secundum Christi doctrinam, vel ut in Christo permaneant. Salutant vos qui mecum sunt fratres, id est cooperatores ac socii mei. Salutant vos omnes sancti in Urbe morantes, maxime autem qui de domo Cæsaris sunt, id est ministri Neronis quos converti, qui et specialem dilectionem ad vos gerunt.
paras.en: [[4:21|Salute ye|Salutate]], that is, wish and speak salvation to, [[4:21|every saint|omnem sanctum]] (Denis reads “all the saints”) belonging to your fellowship, [[4:21|in Christ Jesus|in Christo Jesu]], that is, according to Christ's teaching, or that they may abide in Christ. [[4:22|The brethren who are with me salute you|Salutant vos, qui mecum sunt, fratres]], that is, my fellow workers and companions. [[4:22|All the saints salute you|Salutant vos omnes sancti]], dwelling in the City, [[4:22|especially they that are of Caesar's household|maxime autem qui de Cæsaris domo sunt]], that is, servants of Nero whom I have converted, who also bear a special love towards you.

paras.t: Gratia Domini nostri Jesu Christi sit cum spiritu vestro, id est, in anima vestra, perficiendo ejus essentiam. Amen, id est, sic fiat atque præstetur vobis a Deo sublimi et benedicto.
paras.en: [[4:23|The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit|Gratia Domini nostri Jesu Christi sit cum spiritu vestro]], that is, in your soul, perfecting its essence. [[4:23|Amen|Amen]], that is, so be it done and granted to you by God most high and blessed.
